attributes.morphology: eutectic colonies with sharp cell boundary

evidence.quote: It can be observed that the eutectic colonies grow forming a sharp eutectic cell boundary at the later stage of solidiﬁcation. The average eutectic cell size was w40 mm.
The eutectic spacing was of the order of w600 nm.
But, the average eutectic spacing was decreased signiﬁcantly down to w225 nm, when compared with that in the binary alloy.
The volume fraction of the primary b-Ti dendritic phase was estimated w8% for Ti68Fe28.5In3.5 alloy, and w27% for Ti 66 Fe27 .5In3.5 Nb3 alloy (shown in Table 2).
Moreover, the spacing in the eutectic structure decreased further down to w120 nm.

the enhanced fracture strength and work hardening behavior in Ti 68Fe28.5In3.5 and Ti 66Fe27.5In3.5Nb3 alloys observed in Fig. 4 can be correlated with the internal atomic arrangement of b-Ti solid solution i.e. solid solution hardening by substituting of atoms with different atomic radii

the enhanced fracture strength and work hardening behavior in Ti 68Fe28.5In3.5 and Ti 66Fe27.5In3.5Nb3 alloys observed in Fig. 4 can be correlated with the internal atomic arrangement of b-Ti solid solution i.e. solid solution hardening by substituting of atoms with different atomic radii

Also reﬁnement of eutectic structure by reducing eutectic lamellar spacing generates more interfaces of Ti–Fe (In) and b-Ti phases per unit volume by the addition of small amount of In and then Nb. The increase of Ti–Fe (In) and b-Ti interface per unit volume might be accentuating the role in strengthening the alloys.

Thus, it can be shown that In plays a major role in reﬁning eutectic structure by modifying the growth mode of the eutectic phase, while Nb plays a major role in increasing volume fraction of primary b-Ti phase.
Nb was added as a b phase stabilizer.
Thus the addition of Nb with In in this alloy might be rendering the eutectic growth more sluggish and hence favors the further reﬁnement of lamellar spacing.
